transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me, doctor. Um... I hope I'm doing this right, but... well, I came in mostly because my family and friends think I'm making a big deal out of nothing. I really don't want to sound like I'm just causing trouble, because I'm not, I promise. I just want things to be fair. 

It's just... well, for over a year now, I've known that they're hiding my money. I try to be nice about it, I really do, but I have to keep confronting them, just until they finally tell me the truth. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I don't want you to think badly of me. It's just that they keep showing me these bank papers and saying it proves nothing was taken. But I can see what's happening. I know they're using things like, um, regular bills and fundraisers and plans for trips just to cover it all up. I just want them to be honest with me... it's normal to want that, right?
Do you think it's possible that your family and friends are telling the truth about your money?

I mean... I want to believe them, I really do. I don't want to be a difficult person. I know it probably sounds like I'm just being stubborn, right? I'm sorry if it comes across that way. It's just... no, I don't think they're telling the truth. 

I know they show me those bank statements, and I know they look real... but I've just known for over a year now that they're hiding it. It's like... every time they talk about a new fundraiser, or paying a regular bill, or planning some trip... it's just so obvious to me that they're using all of that to cover up where my money is actually going. I really hate confronting them about it, I promise I do. I just... I have to keep asking until they finally admit it. Does that make sense? I just want to understand why they're doing it. I'm not crazy for wanting them to just be honest, am I?
Have you ever considered the possibility that your belief about your family and friends hiding your money might not be based in reality?

Um... I mean, I really have tried to think about that, because I don't want to be a burden or seem like I'm... you know, making things up. I want to agree with them, I really do. I know I keep bringing up the same things, and I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself... but they just keep saying those bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I've tried to just accept that so everyone will be happy with me. 

But... it's been over a year now, and I just... I know they're hiding it. I can just tell that the regular bills and the fundraisers and the trip plans are just ways to cover it all up. I don't want to be mean to them, but I feel like I have to keep confronting them just until they finally tell the truth. I'm trying my best to be reasonable about it, I promise. Do you... do you think less of me because I can't just let it go?
Have you ever had any moments, no matter how brief, where you doubted your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money?

I... I really wish I could tell you yes, doctor. I know it would make me a lot easier to deal with, and I really, really want to be good about this. I hope you aren't frustrated with me... am I doing okay? 

It's just... no, I haven't ever doubted it. I know I already told you about how they keep showing me those bank papers, saying it proves nothing was taken. And I try so hard to just nod and smile when they do, just so they won't be mad at me... but deep down, I've just known for over a year now that they are hiding my money. I can't un-see it, you know? The regular bills, the fundraisers, the trips they plan... it's all just to cover it up. 

I'm sorry to keep repeating myself, I really am. I don't want to be a bother. I just... I feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell me the truth, because I can't just pretend it isn't happening when I know it is. Does that make me a bad person?
Do you think the way your family and friends are supposedly hiding your money is part of a larger, more complex plot?

Um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I don't sound like I'm trying to make up some big, crazy story... I know how bad that would look, and I really don't want you to think I'm, you know, going off the deep end. I'm trying to be as reasonable as I can be about all of this, I promise. 

It's not like a huge movie plot or anything like that, if that's what you mean. I haven't noticed anything bigger going on at all. It's just my family and my friends, and the things I already told you about... the regular bills and the trips and stuff. I just want them to be honest about my money, that's all. I'm not trying to make it into a bigger deal than it already is, and I don't want to cause any extra trouble. Am I answering your question right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need...
Have you considered that there could be an alternative explanation for the financial situation that doesn't involve your family and friends hiding money from you?

Um... I mean, I really have tried to think about other reasons. I don't want to be difficult, and I know it would be so much easier for everyone if I could just say, "Oh, you're right, there's another explanation." I really want to be agreeable, doctor, I promise. 

But... I just keep coming back to the same thing. I know I've mentioned it before, and I'm sorry to keep bringing it up, but for over a year now, I just know they are hiding it. They show me those bank papers and say it proves nothing is missing, and I try to smile and say okay so they won't be upset with me... but I know what I see. The bills, the fundraisers, the trips... it's all just a way to cover it up. 

I really wish I could just believe another explanation, I do. I don't want to keep confronting them, but I feel like I have to until they just tell the truth. I hope you understand... I'm not trying to be stubborn or make things hard. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you...
Do you think the way your family and friends are hiding your money is somehow unusual or doesn't make sense to other people?

Um... I'm not really sure. I hope it's okay if I just say what I think? I really don't want to sound strange or anything... but no, I don't think it's unusual. It actually seems really normal, the way they do it. 

I mean, they just use regular things, like the bills and the trips I told you about. I don't think it would be hard for other people to understand if they really looked at it, because it's just normal money stuff. I really try hard not to make it sound crazy, because I know how bad that would look, and I want to be a good patient for you. I know I didn't get very far in school, so sometimes I worry I don't explain things the best way... but it just makes sense to me. 

Did I answer that okay? I'm sorry if that wasn't what you were looking for, I just want to make sure I'm doing this right...
Has your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money ever changed or wavered in any way since it started?

Um... no, it hasn't really changed. I hope that's the right answer, I don't want you to think I'm just being difficult or refusing to listen. I really do want to be cooperative. 

But... well, like I said before, it's been over a year now, and I've just known the whole time. I know they keep showing me those bank papers and telling me it proves everything is fine... and I really try to nod and be polite about it so we don't fight. But the feeling just doesn't go away, because I see what they're doing with the bills and the fundraisers and the trips. 

I know it probably sounds bad that I keep bringing it up to them... I really don't like arguing, and I want everyone to just get along. But I feel like I just have to keep confronting them until they finally admit it and tell the truth. I'm sorry if that makes me sound stubborn, I really don't mean to be. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information...
Have you ever considered that you might be wrong about your family and friends hiding your money?

Um... I mean, I really try to be open-minded, doctor. I promise I do. I know it would make everybody so much happier if I just said I was wrong. I hate causing trouble, and I really don't want you to think I'm just being paranoid or... or crazy. I know how that sounds. 

But... well, it's just like I've been saying. I've known for over a year now that they're hiding my money. They keep pointing at those bank papers and telling me it proves nothing was taken, and I really try to just smile and be agreeable so they won't be mad at me. But I see the bills, and the fundraisers, and how they plan those trips... it's all just a way to cover it up. 

I really wish I was wrong, I do. It would be so much easier. But I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth. I'm sorry if that's not what you wanted to hear... I really want to give you the right answers. Does that make sense? I hope you're not upset with me...
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about your family and friends hiding your money?

Um... I really want to say yes, doctor. I promise I do. I know it would be the right thing to say, and I really want to do well in here for you. I hate feeling like I'm being stubborn. 

But... well, it really just goes back to why I came in here in the first place. My family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken... and I try so hard to be nice about it so they don't yell at me, but for over a year now, I've just known they're hiding my money. I can see exactly how they use the bills, and the fundraisers, and the trip plans to cover it all up. 

So because I can see it happening, I don't think I can change my mind... I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth. I'm so sorry, I know I'm probably failing this part of the interview... is it okay that I said that? I just really want to be honest with you.
How much time would you say you spend thinking about your family and friends hiding your money on a typical day?

Um... I'm not really sure how to measure the time, exactly. I hope that's an okay answer. I don't want you to think I'm not paying attention to my own thoughts or anything. I really try to stay focused.

But... well, I guess it's just kind of always there, in the background. Like, I'll be doing the dishes or trying to watch a show, and I just start thinking about the bills and the fundraisers again. I try to push it away so I can just be normal and happy, but it's hard when I know what they're doing. I don't sit around obsessing all day, I promise... I try to stay busy. But it definitely crosses my mind a lot. Is that normal? I mean, for someone in my situation? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a helpful answer...
Do you think other people would agree with you that your family and friends are hiding your money?

Um... I really don't know, doctor. I hope it's okay that I don't have a good answer for that. I mean, I haven't really gone around asking other people about it. I try to keep it quiet because I don't want to make my family look bad, or... or start any drama. I really try to be a good person and not gossip. 

I suppose if someone else saw all the things I see... the way they plan those trips and handle the bills... maybe they would understand? But I don't think anyone else really knows about it. I mostly just keep it to myself, except for when I try to talk to my family about it. I hope that's the right thing to do... I just really don't want to cause a scene. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not being too confusing...
Do you think the way your family and friends are hiding your money is something that could happen to anyone, or is it something unique to you?

Um... oh gosh, I'm really not sure. I hope it's alright that I don't have a very good answer for that one. I... I never really thought about whether it could happen to just anybody. I try to just mind my own business, you know? I want to be polite and not pry into what other people might be going through. 

So I mostly just know that it's happening to me. I really don't want to sound selfish, or like I think I'm, you know, special or anything! I definitely don't think I'm special. I just... I honestly don't know if this kind of thing happens to anyone else, or if it's just unique to my situation. I'm sorry, is that an okay answer? I can try to think about it more if you need me to... I just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.
Do you think there's any possibility that your perception of your family and friends hiding your money could be a mistaken belief?

Um... oh, wow. I really don't want to sound stubborn or... or like I'm not listening to you. I hope you don't think I'm just being difficult. I try so hard to be reasonable and see things from other people's side. 

I know my family and friends keep saying that I'm mistaken. That's actually kind of why I came in... because they keep showing me these bank papers and saying they prove nothing was taken. And I really, really want to just agree with them so everyone can be happy. I hate arguing, I really do. 

But... well, it's been over a year now, and I just... I know they're hiding my money. I can see how they're using the bills, and those fundraisers, and the trip plans to cover it all up. 

I'm so sorry, I know it sounds awful to say that about my own family. I feel terrible even saying it out loud to you, and I'm scared you're going to judge me for it. But I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth. I just want the truth so we can fix it and go back to normal. I hope you can understand why I feel like I have to do that? I'm really not trying to be a bad person or cause trouble, I promise... is it okay that I feel this way?
Do you think your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money could be considered an unreasonable or unfounded idea by others?

Um... oh, I... yes, I guess they probably do think that. I hope you don't think badly of me for it, but... yes. 

I mean, like I was just saying a minute ago, my family and friends keep telling me I'm wrong. They keep bringing out those bank papers and saying they prove nothing was taken at all. So I know they think my ideas are... well, unreasonable. And it hurts my feelings a little, because I really try to be a good person and I don't want them to think I'm crazy or mean. 

But... even though they say those things, it's been over a year now, and I just know they're hiding my money. I can see it in the way they use the bills, and those fundraisers, and the trip plans to cover it all up. I know I'm repeating myself, I'm so sorry! I just... I feel like I have no choice but to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth, even if they think I'm being unreasonable right now. 

I just want everything out in the open so we can all get along again. Is it bad that I can't just let it go? I really hope I'm answering your questions okay... I'm trying my best to explain it right for you.
Do you think your belief about your family and friends hiding your money is something that you might be mistaken about, even if you're completely convinced it's true?

Um... oh, I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just saying the same things over and over to you. I really hope I'm not being frustrating. I want to give you a good answer, I really do. 

I know you're asking if I could be mistaken... and I really, really wish I was. It would be so much easier if I was just confused. That's why I came in, because they keep showing me those bank papers and telling me they prove everything is fine and nothing was taken. And I want to believe them so badly, just to make everyone happy again. 

But... well, it's been over a year now, and I just... I can't ignore what I see. I know they're hiding my money. I see how they use the bills, and the fundraisers, and the trip plans to just... cover it all up. 

I'm so sorry, I know it makes me sound so stubborn, and I really don't want you to think I'm a difficult person. I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth, even if I'm completely convinced... wait, even if *they* think I'm mistaken. I just need the truth so we can fix it. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm making sense for you...
Do you think there's any evidence that could change your mind about your family and friends hiding your money?

Um... oh, wow. That's a really good question. I... I want to say yes, I really do, because I know that's probably what I should say. I hope you don't think I'm just being closed-minded. I try to be open to things, I promise.

But... well, my family and friends, they already try to show me evidence. Like I mentioned, they keep bringing out those bank papers and telling me they prove nothing was taken. And I look at them, I really do, because I want to believe them and just make everything nice again. 

But... it's been over a year of this. And no matter what papers they show me, I just... I know what's happening. I know they're hiding my money. Because I see the other evidence, you know? The way they use the bills, and those fundraisers they talk about, and the plans for trips... it's all just a way to cover it up. 

I'm so sorry, I know I'm saying the same things again, and I probably sound so awful. I hate feeling this way, and I hate confronting them, but I just feel like I have to keep pushing until they finally tell the truth. I just want the truth. I hope you don't think I'm a terrible person for not just accepting their bank papers... I'm really trying to be fair. Did I answer your question okay?
Do you think the idea that your family and friends are hiding your money is a strange or unusual one?

Um... strange? I guess... well, yes, I suppose it might sound a little strange to someone else. I really hope you don't think I'm weird or... or crazy for it. I promise I'm just a normal person otherwise. 

I know I keep saying the same things, and I'm so sorry if I'm boring you or talking in circles. I don't mean to. But... like I mentioned, I really only came in here because they keep waving those bank papers at me, saying they prove absolutely nothing was taken. And maybe it is unusual to think your own family and friends would do something like that... but it's been over a year of this now. I just know they're hiding my money. 

I see all the little things they do, you know? The way they handle the bills, and those fundraisers, and the trip plans they make... I know it's all just to cover it up. I hate fighting with them, I really do. It makes me feel awful to cause trouble. But I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth. 

I just want things to be okay and honest again. Do you think it's too strange that I can't just let it go? I really hope I'm giving you the right kinds of answers... I want to be helpful for you.
Do you think your belief about your family and friends hiding your money is based on facts or just a feeling you have?

Um... oh, I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself again. I really hope you aren't getting annoyed with me. I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. 

Facts or a feeling? I... well, I know it might sound like just a feeling to them. And I really wish it was, I promise I do. Like I said, they keep showing me those bank papers and telling me they prove absolutely nothing was taken, and I'd love to just agree with them and make everyone smile again. 

But... it's not just a feeling. It's been over a year, and I just... I see the facts, even if they don't want to admit it. I know they're hiding my money. The facts are right there in how they handle the bills, and those fundraisers they keep bringing up, and the plans they make for trips. It's all just a way to cover it up, and I can see it. 

I know I probably sound so difficult, and I'm really sorry for that. I don't want to be a burden. I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth. I just want the truth so we can fix things. Is it okay that I see it that way? I really hope I'm making sense and not being too much trouble for you...
